sections.h2: Where is the Wilkes County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is at 500 Court House Drive, Suite 1000, in Wilkesboro, NC 28697. The phone is 336-651-7351, the fax is 336-990-0041, and hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:55 p.m., excluding holidays, per the county's Register of Deeds page.

That is a different building from the Wilkes County Offices on North Street where Tax Administration sits. A seller closing on a Wilkesboro house may need to visit both, or have an attorney handle the recording and request tax figures by phone.

  • Recording and land records: Court House Drive, Suite 1000
  • Tax bills and appeals: 110 North Street
  • Last minute filings: arrive before the 4:55 p.m. close

sections.h2: What does the Wilkes County Register of Deeds keep on file?
sections.html:
The county lists deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, plats, separation agreements, foreclosures, vital records, notary oaths and military discharges. Land records reach back to the formation of the county in 1778.

Birth and death records start in 1913, with some earlier delayed birth entries, and marriage licenses date to 1882. A house with a long chain of title may have its earliest deeds on paper, so ask the office what is indexed and what needs a hand search.

The office records and indexes according to the North Carolina General Statutes. For legal questions about a deed, see an attorney.

sections.h2: Can I search Wilkes County deeds online?
sections.html:
Yes. The office went online on July 1, 2017, and its land records are at wilkesncrod.org, according to the register of deeds page.

The county tax office runs a separate deed search with narrower coverage. It holds copies of the face page and legal description of deeds that the tax office digitized to help its mapping department. Signature and notary pages are generally missing, and deeds of trust, satisfactions and wills are not included.

The Deed Search page states that attorneys and others doing title examinations should not rely on it. Use the register of deeds for anything authoritative, and the clerk of superior court for court records.

sections.h2: What fees apply when recording in Wilkes County?
sections.html:
Recording fees printed in G.S. 161-10, applied by Wilkes County
DocumentFee
General instrument, such as a deed$26.00 up to 15 pages, then $4.00 a page
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 up to 35 pages, then $4.00 a page
Satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgageNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each more
Each extra instrument in one document$10.00

The statute describes the fees as complete and exclusive and says they are collected before filing (G.S. 161-10). Ask the Wilkes office to confirm the schedule at the counter.

sections.h2: How does the deed excise tax work in Wilkes County?
sections.html:
The seller pays one dollar for each five hundred dollars, or fractional part, of the consideration or value of the interest conveyed. Under G.S. 105-228.30, it must be paid to the register of deeds before the instrument is recorded.

Half of the proceeds stays with the county general fund. The other half, less refunds and an allowance, goes to the state each month, and the county may keep 2% of the state's half.

On a gift or low price transfer, the statute looks to value as well as price, so ask the Wilkes office or your attorney what number belongs on the deed.

sections.h2: What should a Wilkes County seller do before recording?
sections.html:
Registration is what protects a new owner. A conveyance or option is not good against lien creditors or buyers who paid value until it is registered in the county where the land lies, and priority follows the time of registration (G.S. 47-18).

  • Confirm any paid off loan has a recorded satisfaction, which carries no fee.
  • Pull the tax figures from Tax Administration so the bill is cleared at closing.
  • Pay the excise tax with the deed.
  • Record the deed first, then the buyer's deed of trust.

Wilkes County's register of deeds is an elected office, with the register chosen by county voters every two years under G.S. 161-1.

sections.h2: What happens in Wilkes County when a house is foreclosed or sold on a land contract?
sections.html:
Foreclosures are among the documents the Wilkes office lists as part of its records. In a North Carolina power of sale foreclosure the sale is not final on auction day: an upset bid must beat the last price by at least 5%, with a $750.00 minimum increase, and each bid opens another 10 day period (G.S. 45-21.27).

Owners who sold on a contract for deed should know the seller must record the contract, or a memorandum of it, within five business days under Chapter 47H. A buyer on such a contract has three business days to cancel.

If the lender or buyer defaults, forfeiture needs a written default notice with a cure date at least 30 days after service. Anyone selling a Wilkes County property that carries one of these arrangements should have an attorney review the recorded papers first.

sections.h2: Can long possession give someone title to Wilkes County land?
sections.html:
North Carolina allows title by adverse possession after 20 years of possession under known and visible lines and boundaries, adverse to everyone else (G.S. 1-40). That rule matters on old rural tracts, where boundaries come from deeds that go back generations.

If a neighbor has used part of your land for decades, a deed search at the register of deeds shows what is recorded, and a survey shows where the lines fall. Sort that out before you list, because a buyer's title search will find any recorded claim.

  • Order a survey if lines are uncertain
  • Pull the vesting deed and check the legal description
  • Ask your attorney about unrecorded claims

sections.h2: What happens to tenants and occupants when a Wilkes County house changes hands?
sections.html:
For a foreclosure sale of residential property with fewer than 15 rental units, the notice of sale must say an order for possession may issue. Tenants under leases entered or renewed on or after October 1, 2007 may end the lease on at least 10 and no more than 90 days' notice after the sale date (G.S. 45-21.16A).

In an ordinary sale, a tenant's lease terms are a matter for the contract and the buyer's lender. Give the closing office a copy of every lease, and ask whether any month to month tenant needs a notice to quit before closing.

  • Month to month tenancy: seven days' notice to quit
  • Week to week: two days
  • Year to year: one month or more before the year ends

Those notice periods come from G.S. 42-14. None of this requires a recording at the Wilkes office, but a recorded memorandum is needed for a lease longer than three years to bind later buyers.

faqs.q: What are the Wilkes County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:55 p.m., excluding holidays. The office is at 500 Court House Drive, Suite 1000, in Wilkesboro, and the phone is 336-651-7351.

faqs.q: Is there a website for Wilkes County land records?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says its land records have been online at wilkesncrod.org since July 1, 2017. The tax office also has a limited deed copy search, which is not meant for title work.

faqs.q: How far back do Wilkes County land records go?
faqs.a: To the formation of the county in 1778. Birth and death records start in 1913 and marriage licenses in 1882, according to the register of deeds page.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Wilkes County deed?
faqs.a: The seller pays the excise tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. The statute sets it at one dollar per five hundred dollars or fractional part of the value conveyed.

faqs.q: Does recording a mortgage satisfaction cost anything in Wilkes County?
faqs.a: No. State law sets no fee for recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage.
